subsystems.name: System-on-chip
subsystems.role: combines CPU, GPU, and NPU on one die, with a wide memory controller.

subsystems.name: Unified memory
subsystems.role: provides a single high-bandwidth pool shared by CPU and GPU so large models stay resident.

subsystems.name: Storage
subsystems.role: holds the operating system and model weights, loading them quickly at startup.

subsystems.name: Thermal system
subsystems.role: removes heat from the SoC during sustained inference.

subsystems.name: Power delivery
subsystems.role: converts mains power into stable low voltages for the SoC and memory.

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: runs quantised models efficiently on the available hardware.

buildSteps.title: Design the SoC
buildSteps.detail: Chip architects choose CPU, GPU, and NPU cores and a memory controller wide enough to feed them from a unified pool.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the chip
buildSteps.detail: The design is manufactured at a foundry on an advanced process node, then tested and binned.

buildSteps.title: Package memory
buildSteps.detail: LPDDR chips are soldered onto the same package or board, close to the SoC, to keep traces short and bandwidth high.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the mainboard
buildSteps.detail: Surface-mount machines place the SoC, memory, power regulators, and connectors onto a small printed circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Build the cooling
buildSteps.detail: A heatsink, heat pipes or vapor chamber, and a fan are fitted to carry heat away from the SoC.

buildSteps.title: Final assembly
buildSteps.detail: The mainboard, SSD, and I/O ports are mounted in the enclosure, and cables are connected.

buildSteps.title: Test and image
buildSteps.detail: Each unit is stress-tested for thermals and performance, then flashed with firmware and an OS image preloaded with an inference runtime.

buildSteps.title: Ship
buildSteps.detail: The finished mini PC is boxed with documentation and power supply.

prerequisites.why: let CPU and GPU share the same large pool, which is what keeps big models resident.
shrinks model weights to 4-bit or 8-bit so they fit in available memory and run faster.
software such as llama.cpp or ONNX Runtime maps model operations onto the available CPU, GPU, and NPU.
memory bandwidth, not raw compute, is usually the bottleneck for local inference.
allows memory to be placed very close to the SoC, reducing latency and power.

pathway.milestone: mini PCs with tens of gigabytes of unified memory run models with up to tens of billions of parameters at usable speeds.
pathway.unlocks: private, offline AI for individuals and small teams.

pathway.milestone: unified memory pools grow to hundreds of gigabytes and bandwidth increases with LPDDR6 and wider buses.
pathway.unlocks: running the largest open models locally without cloud.

pathway.milestone: NPUs and GPUs become better integrated with standard APIs and compilers.
pathway.unlocks: faster, more power-efficient inference and easier deployment.

pathway.milestone: on-device fine-tuning and multi-modal models become practical on a desktop box.
pathway.unlocks: personalised AI that never leaves the owner's hardware.
